extra.reason: Fixed. A followed chain now answers the question the option asks in bytes: the engine keeps the wire truth (RedirectHop.RequestRaw/ResponseRaw, Response.Raw on the final response; hop requests rendered once so the scope gate authorises exactly the bytes the transport writes, hops sent via SendAs under the same rules as the operator's own send), the web layer maps them onto repeaterHop.request/response riding the send's own response, and the Repeater pane offers First/Final response plus per-hop 'View response' in the chain table — the chain is additive,  stays the operator's own. Follow-up fix the new tests caught: redirectRequest advertised the hop's Host as the bare hostname, dropping a non-default port — contradicts Burp's decompiled Zxrb.Zv authority rendering (host only for https/443 and http/80, host:port otherwise, IPv6 bracketed; :authority rewritten per hop on h2) and RFC 9112 3.2; hostPortFor now mirrors it. Evidence: sender tests TestAFollowedHopKeepsTheBytesItSentAndReceived / TestAnUnfollowedHopCarriesNoBytes / TestTheRawEntryKeepsTheFirstResponseBytesOnFinal, web test TestRepeaterServesTheChainHopsBytesAlongsideTheSend + byteless-refused-hop assertions; go build/vet/gofmt clean, whole-tree go test 38 pkgs ok, e2e-go.sh 24/0, e2e-ui 157 unit + axe green — e2e-ui's 8 failing specs fail identically at HEAD (bisected in a separate worktree) and are filed separately.

Fixed: all 8 failing specs resolved and the fixes verified manually in a real browser (agent-browser) as requested. Root causes: (1) RepeaterPage rendered hooks after its empty-state return — 'Rendered more hooks than during the previous render' killed every fresh-browser flow (5 specs); hooks moved unconditional, a4dd7d5. (2) renderTabTrigger's ContextMenu wrapper had no key — React unkeyed-children console error the suite asserts against (1 spec); keyed on tab id, a4dd7d5. (3) dock-persistence spec used a '.editor' class that exists nowhere (editor root is editor-shell) — spec fix 0a41a14. (4) proxyGet was describe-scoped but called from another describe — ReferenceError; moved to module scope, 0a41a14. (5) in-scope-only spec asserted an empty-state string the product never rendered ('this filter' vs 'these filters') — spec fix, 0a41a14. (6) decoder spec clicked Add inside a collapsed empty section; now expands first, 0a41a14. Product fix discovered by manual testing: a typed history query matching nothing claimed 'No traffic captured yet' while a seeded capture sat behind it — the typed query was not in activeFilterNames; now named, verified live in the browser ('No exchange matches these filters ... query host = ...'), a4dd7d5. Note: full playwright suite was interrupted at 218/1 (decoder spec) before the expand-first spec fix; unit suites green throughout (go 38 pkgs, UI 157).

Forward all shipped: engine ForwardAll (mirrors DropAll once-only gate + single signal, forwards held bytes unmodified — nil would wake the client to an empty message), POST /api/intercept/forward-all answering the honest count, toolbar button between Forward and Drop all with the queue-moved toast, no confirmation needed for the safe direction. Verified manually in agent-browser: 3 held -> one click -> queue empty, clients unblocked with own bytes, history rows present. Engine test TestEngine_ForwardAllForwardsEveryHeldMessageUnmodifiedAndCountsOnlyItsOwn, web tests, route manifest, UI unit 157/0 green. Commits: see forward-all commit on ui-react-comparison.

Shipped in 7b29220: Pretty view is editable; every keystroke writes back through compactMessage (message.ts), which inverts the prettifier — JSON re-stringified minified, markup collapsed back to the inter-tag breaks prettyMarkup inserted, head kept byte-identical, mid-edit JSON parse failure passes the operator's text through unchanged. The wire bytes, Raw and Hex all agree with the compacted body, so the 'reformatted body is not the bytes sent' objection no longer applies. Tests: 6 new compactMessage contract tests in message.test.ts (Pretty edit round-trips to minified bytes; edited head preserved verbatim; mid-edit JSON pass-through; pure-tag markup round-trips byte-identically and is a prettyMessage fixed point; multi-line text-node newlines preserved; non-formattable body untouched). bun run check: 163 pass / 0 fail / 354 expect. Go gate clean.

Shipped in 7b29220: an unchosen editor (initial state 'raw' means 'operator has not chosen') now opens on Pretty whenever canPretty — Burp's documented default (tools/message-editor/text-editor.html: 'By default, messages are displayed in the Pretty tab whenever Burp detects a supported format'). The first explicit click, including a click back to Raw, wins for the pane's life via pickedRef — same deal Burp gives a pane once the operator has expressed a preference. A message whose Pretty view disappears falls back to Raw. bun run check: 163 pass / 0 fail.

Fixed in b012797: the nav.palette note in shortcuts.ts:82 claimed 'Burp ships its palette with no default binding at all' — false; Burp's documented default is Ctrl+K, which burpsy already binds (defaultChord: mod+k, unchanged). The note now reads 'Burp's documented default is also Ctrl+K, so this matches Burp exactly'. One-line change; bun run check: 163 pass / 0 fail / 354 expect.

Fixed: the claim was inverted. cmd/desktop/main.go IS a working Wails v2 shell with a native File/View/Tools/Help menu bar (buildMenu, main.go:151-203), native dialogs, and the console UI served via reverse-proxy AssetServer; verified it builds at HEAD (go build ./cmd/desktop). reference.ts's 'A desktop shell' entry said 'No native window and no system tray' — the no-tray half was true, the no-window half was false. The entry now states the shipped reality. bun run check 163/0.

Fixed in e8a8396: the status bar now renders the proxy listener address (stats.data.proxy_bind) as a live fact beside stored/exchanges/messages. Proven interactively on the live console (browser-driven, not Playwright): status bar displays '127.0.0.1:18200' matching the -proxy flag. bun run check 163/0.

Fixed in e8a8396: two affordances keep the empty-state promise — (a) clicking the already-selected connection deselects it (ConnectionRow toggle with aria-pressed), (b) a 'Clear connection selection' X button in the detail head whenever a connection is selected but no frame is. Proven interactively: relayed two real WebSocket upgrades through the proxy to a local origin, selected a connection (frames filtered), clicked clear (all 4 frames visible again), clicked the same connection twice (deselects). bun run check 163/0.

Closed STALE: the claim predates the held-row menu expansion. intercept.tsx:473-607 heldMenu() now offers Send to Repeater (copies row.raw to a Repeater tab without resolving the hold), Send to Comparer A/B, Send to Decoder, Copy URL/curl/to-file, Add host to scope, Open in browser, plus Forward/Drop. Only the Intruder handoff is absent, and :459-461 documents why it is deliberate: Intruder splices into a stored message id, which a held message does not have. Verified against HEAD 325905b by source read; no code change needed.

Implemented per the issue's option 2: Intruder consumes internal/bcheck's enumerator instead of growing a second parser. JSON bodies now offer one body_json_value position per string value (numbers/booleans excluded, matching Burp), payloads JSON-escaped so the document survives; base64/XML nested containers in body values arrive as body_nested_value with the outer wire value rebuilt per payload. Form bodies keep the existing wire-faithful walker; XML/multipart keep the entire-body fallback until bcheck models them (single-parser policy). Side effect: fixed a latent scanner bug — nestedDecode treated nestedBase64JSON as identity while nestedEncode re-encoded, so Apply corrupted doubly-encoded values; regression test added. Full intruder/bcheck/core suites pass; scanner runtime-coverage passes with the change.

Payload column shipped and verified: every attempt row the server returns names its payload combination — resolved server-side via payloadsAt over the post-processing-rule sets (Examples now covers attempt ordinals, not just bucket first-ordinals, bounded by the existing detail limit), rendered in the Results Attempts table as the second column per Burp's documented layout, with a browser-side ordinal-arithmetic fallback for ordinals the server could not place. UI lib tests (172), type check, Go web tests and a rebuilt bundle all verified. Blocked dependents pf4 (CSV export) and 4rd (sortable tables) stay open.

MayContainHost now applies Contains' include semantics: empty include list means everything, non-empty is an allow-list that refuses a host matching no rule. Pinned by TestMayContainHostRefusesAHostMatchingNoIncludeRule (internal/core/scope_may_contain_host_test.go) and TestEveryGroupSendModeRefusesAHostMatchingNoIncludeRule (internal/web/api_repeater_group_test.go). Committed 0d3e656.

DELETE /api/history with {ids} or no body (Clear); tombstone map on TrafficStore keeps positional ids stable; UI gets tick column + Delete items + Clear with confirm modal. Unit tests in internal/core/store_delete_test.go, e2e in behaviour.spec.ts 'History delete and clear'. Committed 0d3e656; e2e-ui suite 228 passed.

Filter bar with MIME buckets (html/json/xml/javascript/css/image), status-class buckets (2xx/3xx/4xx/5xx) and request-type toggles (in-scope, requested-only, parameterized-only, hide not-found). Server: Exchange.Mime folds into PathNode.Mimes and unions up the tree (sitemap_mime_test.go). UI: boolean axes per-node, set axes subtree-aware. e2e: 2xx keeps tree, 4xx empties with honest empty-state, Clear restores. Commit + e2e 'site map' 3 passed.

DELETE /api/sitemap with {host,port,tls,path,kind}: kind=host|branch|item. Recorded decision: removal is SUPPRESSION (sitemap.SiteMap.Suppress) — the projection drops the branch and it stays out across Sync rebuilds and re-captures; underlying exchanges untouched so history/findings/audit references stay whole. No undo by design (re-capture repopulates; restart rebuilds). Tests: 4 sitemap unit (host/branch/item semantics incl. /apiary segment boundary + survives-Sync), 2 web (named 400 refusals, store-stays-whole), 1 e2e (right-click, confirm modal with honest copy, rows gone, sibling /r10e-other survives). Manifest: riskDestructive with reasoning. Commit 3bd6f43.

Tree rows now carry a right-click menu aimed at the NODE: Add <host> to scope (POST /api/scope include + scope cache invalidation), Passively scan this host/branch (usePassiveScanBranch, sends nothing), Actively scan this host/branch (crawl) seeded from the node URL with retention_query composed like crawlFrom (host= or path~prefix/), plus 10e's Delete host/branch/item. Menu builds from FlatRow's resolved host (node.segment is the last segment and would no-op). e2e: asserts the three node-aimed items on a right-clicked row and drives add-to-scope through the real API reading scope rules back. Commit ebe11bd. Expand/collapse-branch menu items deliberately left: the flatten pass already auto-expands filtered branches; recursive manual expand is a separate concern.

Task detail gains an Issue activity tab: reverse-chronological findings (by id, the store's dense counter), each row naming severity (same findingTone mapping as Issues/sitemap), issue name and host, times_seen shown as ×N. 'Open' sets a new session-only issueFocus store flag (consumed like History's focusExchange: read/act/clear) and routes to Issues, which selects the finding's first leaf and expands its host+path branch so the advisory is actually visible. Feed reads the same /api/issues cache key the Issues page uses, so mid-scan findings appear without a second request. e2e: seeded audit -> feed row names severity/host -> Open lands on Issues advisory. Commit fc08b1d.

Task tiles carry a kebab menu with Scan again and Delete task. Routes: POST /api/tasks/{id}/again (crawl re-runs through the same startCrawl the New scan dialog uses; other kinds answer 409 naming why — the row doesn't carry an audit's exchange id or an attack's payload set); DELETE /api/tasks/{id} (dash.Registry.Delete refuses a RUNNING task -> 409 'cancel first'; unknown id 404; no UI confirm because the row is state about past work — findings/exchanges/coverage survive). Manifest keeps the subtree riskLocal with the row-vs-evidence reasoning. Synthesised standing live-audit tile gets no menu (no registry row). Tests: 2 web (re-run starts a real running crawl; delete semantics incl. running-task refusal leaving the work running), 1 e2e (seeded audit deleted end to end). Pause/resume deliberately not here — that is 8gw. Commit 277d698.

Render tab now covers image responses (image/* via data URL over an , centred, never upscaled, same white stage as the HTML iframe). Byte-exactness required a wire change: MessageView gains body_base64 — the body's exact octets base64-encoded, populated only for non-UTF-8 bodies (JSON strings destroy bytes like PNG's 0x89 into U+FFFD; text alone would render a different image). HttpEditor takes bodyBase64 and prefers it. Tests: 2 web (exact-bytes round-trip; omit for UTF-8 bodies), 1 bun unit, 1 e2e driving a real 2x2 PNG through the proxy and asserting the PNG magic bytes in the rendered data URL — fails against pre-fix code (0x89 arrived as 0xFD). Commit ae5ed32.

Read-only editors route the six codec transforms through showTransform: selection read, result shown in a modal with the output in a <pre>, Copy-and-close, and the honest subtitle 'the message is read-only, so the conversion is shown here instead of written in place'. Editable editors keep the in-place path; both share the same transform functions. e2e drives it on a history row: double-click 'deep', Base64-encode via Actions menu, dialog shows ZGVlcA== (proves the transform ran on the real selection), close. Note: a non-editable CodeMirror ignores keyboard selection movement — the test selects by mouse. Commit 656b9a5.

POST /api/session/rules/{id}/test: session.RunMacroDetailed dry-runs the rule's steps with the same loop as RunMacro (interpolation, scope gating, jar cookie threading, extraction, validity) and reports per step: sent form (post-interpolation, with sent_cookie), response, set_cookies, and every extraction's outcome (resolved or not, with detail). Skipped steps name why ('out of scope' / send error). Deliberately NOT /run: writes nothing to the login-run memory so update-macro cannot promote a test (pinned by web test). Wire DTO lowercases StepResult fields (untagged StepResult would leak 'Status' which TypeScript reads as undefined — casing tripwire asserted in test). UI: Test macro button on rule editor (needs saved rule) + per-step report with extraction table and response body. Tripwire: session test runs one scenario through BOTH entry points and requires agreement. Tests: 3 session, 3 web. Manifest /test under rule subtree riskCredential.

ScopeRule gained Enabled (defaults true in NewScopeRule so the zero value can never disable excludes and fail scope open), gated in Matches — the single point MayContainHost and MatchesRequest both pass through. POST /api/scope gained the 'toggle' action matching RemoveScoped's exact tuple identity; GET reports enabled on every row. scope_rules_v3 carries an enabled column (NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 via addColumn; every pre-column row was active), round-trip pinned by TestRestoreKeepsAScopeRulesDisabledState. Engine tests: TestDisablingAnIncludeRuleTakesItsHostsOutOfScope, TestDisablingAnExcludeRuleLetsItsHostsBackIn (with the include list admitting the host — exclude-wins semantics are not overridden by the toggle), TestMayContainHostSeesADisabledRuleTheSameWayContainsDoes, TestSetRuleEnabledMatchesTheTupleExactly. API tests: disable/re-enable loop, exclude direction, 404 on a nonexistent tuple. Scope page has the Enabled checkbox column wired to toggle. Verified live: toggle→enabled:false persists across a server restart and the Repeater send to that host is refused while disabled. Commit 85b0b63.

core.Scope gained dropOutOfScope (seed off), enforced at AuthoriseRequest and AuthoriseRaw — the two places a request is actually issued. AuthoriseRaw's refusal says 'dropped: ...' so egress is distinguishable from retention. Deliberately NOT wired into MayContainHost: filtering its include loop on Enabled returns default-allow when every include is disabled, the opposite of Contains — that would re-open the cj7x disagreement; the doc comment records why. GET /api/scope reports drop_out_of_scope; POST action drop_out_of_scope flips it (nil enabled refused 400). Persisted via settings key scope.drop_out_of_scope, restored in Store.Restore beside the rules. Scope page has Burp's 'Out-of-scope request handling' card with the checkbox. Tests: TestDropOutOfScope* (engine, incl. disabled-includes and excludes-win), TestAuthoriseRawNamesTheDrop/KeepsThePlainRefusal, TestMayContainHostIsUnchangedByTheDropSwitch, TestRestoreKeepsTheDropOutOfScopeSwitch (persist), TestTheDropOutOfScopeSwitchRoundTripsThroughTheAPI + refusal test (web). Verified live: proxied request to an unscoped host refused with the switch on; switch survives restart. Commit 2173be9.

WebSocket history frame list narrows by direction, opcode and payload substring — server-side on /api/ws/history (new direction/opcode/payload params; payload read through WsPayload per candidate because the bytes are not on the row; unknown direction/opcode refused 400 rather than ignored, matching the exchange param's rule). UI gains the toolbar (direction, opcode, debounced substring, clear-when-set) and the empty state distinguishes 'no frames match the filters' from 'no frames on this connection' from 'nothing captured yet'. Query key carries all three axes so cache entries cannot cross views. Bambda framing not reintroduced, per 8sa. Tests: TestWsHistoryFiltersByDirectionOpcodeAndPayload, TestWsHistoryRefusesUnknownFilterValues. Committed b4ad874.

useMessageLayout + MessageLayoutSwitch in ui/layout.tsx: horizontal / vertical / combined, persisted per surface under burpsy.layout.<storageId> (same localStorage contract as SplitPane's divider), defaulting to each surface's prior hardcoded orientation. History (highest-frequency surface) wired first: the annotate bar carries the three-icon radiogroup; combined renders the pair as Request/Response Tabs with one mounted editor and the grid collapses to one track so the Inspector keeps its column. Verified live against the running binary: horizontal side-by-side with Inspector, combined single-pane tabs, vertical default, choice survives reload (pressed icon + grid class restored). Remaining pages take the same hook with no new design. Commit a11f255.

SequencerReport gained extra_stats (chi_square, serial_correlation + caveat label, monte_carlo_pi/deviation, repeated_tokens + repeated_list) computed by extraFor() sharing the engine's own ChiSquare/SerialCorrelation/MonteCarloPi/DetectPatterns — the two front-ends now read one set of numbers. Serial correlation is labelled in the JSON itself as 'not Burp's bit-position correlation test' so the conflation the issue warns about cannot happen silently. The Sequencer page gains the 'Uniformity & duplicates' card; repeated tokens lead and go warn-toned when non-zero. Tests: TestReportCarriesTheDuplicateTokenCount, TestReportShowsZeroDuplicatesForDistinctTokens, TestReportCarriesChiSquareAndItRisesWithSkew (uniform → exactly 0 per expected=total/distinct semantics, skewed → larger), TestSerialCorrelationLabelNamesTheCaveat, TestReportCarriesMonteCarloPi. Verified live: POST /api/sequencer/analyse returns extra_stats with the duplicate named; card renders. Commit 1da4916.

POST /api/sequencer/capture/pause and /resume hold the newest live capture between sends (never inside one — the in-flight send records whole). The wire's paused flag is the loop's own pausedAtGate, not the handler's request: the one send already on the wire when pause lands still records, and a sample growing 'while paused' is the lie the flag-split avoids (found by the test racing it). 409 when nothing runs or the capture finished; GET refused like stop. Copy tokens / Save tokens ride the view's existing token list (no new route); UI gains Pause/Resume (Play/Pause icons) and both export buttons, guarded on an empty sample. Tests: TestACaptureCanBePausedAndResumedWithoutLosingTokens (freeze + no loss + resume growth), TestPausingWithNoLiveCaptureIsRefused, TestCaptureViewCarriesTheTokensForExport (non-empty, no blank tokens). Verified live: 12→12 frozen across 1s, 12→21 after resume, paused flag accurate. Commit 2237cfd.

Issues filter bar rebuilt as Burp's combinable checkbox groups: 'Show only' severity (5) and confidence (3) over Set<string> — empty set means no constraint, non-empty is an allow-list, so High+Medium shows together. Hide-false-positive checkbox rides the existing false_positive wire flag (no backend change; the tree already dims FPs). Empty state counts any active filter. Verified live with seeded findings: High alone 1, +Medium 5, +hide-FP 4, cleared 5; FP row dimmed throughout. Commit d11fcce. (hide-duplicate not built: findings already merge into one row with occurrences — there is no duplicate row to hide; the merge IS the dedup.)

POST /api/issues/record creates a hand-recorded finding attached to one exchange: first-class (same store/triage/persistence), confidence defaults Certain (operator saw it — stronger than any scanner), severity defaults Low (ungraded must not inflate High), exchange_id is *uint64 because exchange 0 is real (dense counters from zero). Same-name+host records merge via ordinary dedup — Burp's 'adds to a previously created issue'. Comment rides the Triage path (operator state, one write path). UI: 'Record an issue' in Engagement tools of the shared row/editor menu, three prompts, issues list invalidated. Route pinned riskLocal in the manifest. Tests: TestAnIssueCanBeRecordedByHandAgainstAnExchange, TestARecordedIssueDefaults*, TestARecordedIssueWithoutADescriptionNamesItsExchange, TestARecordedIssueCarriesTheOperatorsComment, TestRecordingAgainstAMissingExchangeIsRefused, TestASecondRecordWithTheSameNameMergesIntoTheFirst. Verified live: curl record (id 10, Medium/Certain, exchange 4) and UI context-menu record ('Issue #11 recorded against #4'). Commit b3d6b63.
